---
title: "Explore forward propagation"
toc: false
page-layout: full
---

A neural network does not assign a fixed label to an input point. Its current
weights and biases define a function that maps an input to a probability. In
this two-input, three-hidden-unit network, edit the input and all thirteen trainable
parameters to see that function change.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to watch

The labeled dots are a toy binary-classification dataset. The colored plane
shows the network's current predicted probability, which need not match those
labels because these parameters have not been trained. Click the plane or edit
the selected input, then change a parameter and observe both the probability
region and the forward-pass calculation.
:::

```{=html}
<div id="nn-forward-explorer" class="nn-forward-explorer" aria-label="Interactive neural-network forward propagation explorer">
  <div class="nn-forward-toolbar clt-buttons">
    <button id="nn-animate" type="button" class="regression-sampling-primary">Animate forward pass</button>
    <button id="nn-reset" type="button">Reset example</button>
    <output id="nn-status" class="nn-forward-status" aria-live="polite">Ready</output>
  </div>

  <div class="nn-forward-workbench">
    <aside class="nn-workbench-panel nn-parameter-panel" aria-labelledby="nn-parameter-heading">
      <div class="nn-workbench-heading">
        <h2 id="nn-parameter-heading">Parameters</h2>
        <p>Set all weights and biases.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="nn-parameter-workspace">
        <div id="nn-parameter-controls" class="nn-parameter-controls" aria-label="Neural-network parameter controls"></div>
      </div>
    </aside>

    <section class="nn-workbench-panel nn-network-panel" aria-labelledby="nn-network-heading">
      <div class="nn-workbench-heading nn-network-heading">
        <div>
          <h2 id="nn-network-heading">Forward pass</h2>
          <p>Matching colors link each parameter row to the connections it controls; line thickness shows the magnitude of the corresponding weight.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="nn-forward-controls">
        <div id="nn-input-controls" class="nn-input-controls" aria-label="Selected input controls"></div>
        <div id="nn-dataset-controls" class="nn-dataset-controls" aria-label="Toy dataset controls"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="nn-network-stage">
        <figure class="nn-forward-figure nn-architecture-figure">
          <svg id="nn-network-diagram" role="img" aria-label="Two-input, three-hidden-unit, one-output neural network"></svg>
        </figure>
        <figure class="nn-forward-figure nn-probability-figure">
          <svg id="nn-probability-plane" role="img" aria-label="Toy binary-classification observations and predicted positive-label probability in the x₁–x₂ input plane"></svg>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </section>
  </div>
</div>
```

The positive region on the plane is the **model's** current predicted-positive
region, using the default decision threshold of $0.5$. It is not a ground-truth
label map. In the next lesson, backpropagation will explain how the parameters
can be adjusted to reduce loss on labeled observations.
